deep.reconstruction:
This page continues the list (items a–g on p.3) of the structures a 'homotopy theory' H should carry. It is a programmatic catalogue written just before Grothendieck starts axiomatising 'théories de variance homotopique' (the derivators) on the next page.

Item h) asks whether one can define K-theoretic invariants K(H) of a homotopy theory from its 'triangles exacts', or even higher K-groups K_i ('voire K supérieurs'). In modern terms this is the question of the algebraic K-theory of a homotopy theory, i.e. of a model category, derivator or ∞-category, rather than of an exact or triangulated category. He asks: 'Cas additif seulement?!?' In other words, does this only make sense in the additive or stable setting? Modern answer:
- K_0 can be defined from distinguished triangles in the triangulated case.
- Higher K-theory needs more than the triangulated category (Schlichting 2002). It is defined via Waldhausen's S-construction (Waldhausen 1983/85), which needs only a pointed category with cofibrations and weak equivalences. So it is not strictly additive: A(X) is built from retractive spaces.
- Its dependence on the underlying homotopy theory was settled by Toën–Vezzosi (2004) and Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada (2013).
- In derivator language: Maltsiniotis, 'La K-théorie d'un dérivateur triangulé' (2007), followed by Garkusha and Muro–Raptis.

The item labelled h_f (relabelled i?; an arrow links it to h), possibly a reordering) records frequent extra structure:
- internal Hom objects Hom(x,y) in H, with Hom(x,y) = Γ Hom(x,y), where Γ (or π0) : H → Ens is an important functor, typically Hom(1,−) for a unit object 1;
- a multiplicative structure (cartesian product or ⊗) with the closed-monoidal adjunction Hom(x⊗y,z) ≅ Hom(x, Hom(y,z)).
The dated margin note (24.11.83) asks how these internal Homs relate to the external 'Hom with values in Hot' from item e) on the previous page. Today this is the relation Map(x,y) ≃ Map(1, Hom(x,y)) between enriched mapping spaces and internal Hom in a closed monoidal ∞-category or monoidal model category.

The final paragraph observes that, except perhaps for structures f) (truncations) and g) (invariants Π_i, H_i), everything seems derivable from the pair (M, W ⊂ Fl(M)): a category with a class of weak equivalences, Grothendieck's later 'localizer'. The programme is to isolate the right axioms. This is the philosophy realised by Dwyer–Kan simplicial localisation (1980) and later by relative categories and ∞-categories, and in Grothendieck's own Pursuing Stacks and Les Dérivateurs.
errors: No mathematical errors. The doubt about f) and g) is well-founded: in the stable case, truncations and homology functors with values in an abelian 'heart' require extra data (a t-structure, BBD 1982). They are not determined by (M,W) alone. In the unstable case, Postnikov truncations and homotopy groups are intrinsic.

The 'additive only?' worry is partly right and partly wrong. A triangulated structure alone does not determine higher K-theory (Schlichting). However, Waldhausen K-theory needs only a pointed homotopy theory with cofibrations, not additivity.

ideas.what: K-theory (K_0 via exact triangles, and higher K_i) as an invariant of an abstract homotopy theory H, with the question whether it is restricted to the additive case
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic K-theory of Waldhausen categories / stable ∞-categories / triangulated derivators
ideas.usually_credited_to: Waldhausen (1983–85); Thomason–Trobaugh (1990); Toën–Vezzosi (2004); Maltsiniotis (2007, derivators); Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada (2013)
ideas.where_published: Possibly hinted at in Pursuing Stacks / Les Dérivateurs; Maltsiniotis' K-theory of derivators develops it in Grothendieck's framework

ideas.what: Internal Hom in the homotopy category with Hom = Γ∘Hom, Γ = Hom(1,−) or π0
ideas.modern_name: Closed (symmetric) monoidal homotopy category; global sections of internal mapping object

ideas.what: Tensor–Hom adjunction Hom(x⊗y,z) ≅ Hom(x, Hom(y,z)) in H; relation of internal Hom to the Hot-valued external Hom
ideas.modern_name: Closed monoidal ∞-category; compatibility of enrichment (mapping spaces) with internal Hom

ideas.what: Everything except possibly truncations and Π_i/H_i should be expressible in terms of (M, W ⊂ Fl(M)); isolate the right axioms
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy theory = localizer / relative category; invariance under Dwyer–Kan localization

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly listed K-theory, including higher K-groups, as an invariant to be defined for an abstract homotopy theory, in late 1983 at the birth of the derivator programme. He also questioned whether it is confined to the additive case. This predates or parallels Waldhausen's published framework and anticipates Maltsiniotis' derivator K-theory and the later invariance question.
missed.quote: Possibilité de définir des invariants K(H) via "triangles exacts", voire K supérieurs d'une théorie homotopique. (Cas additif seulement?!?)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical. It documents that K-theory of derivators (Maltsiniotis 2007) was part of Grothendieck's own 1983 programme. The 'non-additive?' question connects to unstable/Waldhausen-type K-theory of pointed homotopy theories in derivator language, which is still less developed than the stable case.

missed.claim: He suspects truncations and homotopy/homology invariants valued in abelian categories may NOT be determined by the localizer (M,W). This matches the modern fact that, in the stable case, these require a t-structure as extra data.
missed.quote: Sauf peut-être les structures f) et g)), il semble que tout puisse se décrire en termes de (M, W⊂Fl(M))
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It is a correct early intuition separating intrinsic structure from extra structure, but it is well understood today.

deep.surprise_reason: Programmatic list; mostly standard structures (closed monoidal homotopy categories, localizers). The notable detail is the explicit 1983 wish for (higher) K-theory of an abstract homotopy theory and the doubt about additivity. This is interesting historically but was followed up (Waldhausen, Maltsiniotis, Toën–Vezzosi, Blumberg–Gepner–Tabuada).
transcription_corrections: 'voir K-[?] supérieurs' likely reads 'voire K_i supérieurs' (or 'voire K supérieurs').
'{+ou+} un foncteur important' should be 'ou un foncteur important'.
Margin 'Hom_Prot(x,y) ∈ Ob Hst dans c) ??' more plausibly reads 'Hom_Hot(x,y) ∈ Ob Hot dans e) ??', referring to the Hot-valued external Hom of item e) on the previous page.
'il semble que tout provient à dérivier en termes de' should probably read 'il semble que tout puisse se décrire (ou se déduire) en termes de'.
The item label 'h_f)' is an overwritten label (probably f/h → i), with an arrow linking it to the item at the top; the top label also seems overwritten (h).
